```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

You've written an R function that wraps a command line tool.
Its help page says "see `mri_convert --help` for the full list of options", and every user who reads that line has to leave R, open a terminal, and hope the tool on their `PATH` is the one your function will call.

The obvious fix is to paste the tool's help into your roxygen block.
That works until the tool's next release, when your copy quietly goes stale.
The help you want is the help of the tool _the user_ has installed, generated when they open the page.

R can do that.
Rd files support `\Sexpr[stage=render]`, a macro that runs R code each time a help page is displayed.
ventro provides the R code to put inside it.

```{r}
#| label: load
library(ventro)
```

## Why not just call the tool?

Here is roughly what you might write first: run the tool, paste its output into the page.
We'll use a made-up line of help text that looks like plenty of real ones.

```{r}
#| label: raw-help
raw_help <- "Usage: tool [--format=%d] {input} [output]"
```

```{r}
#| label: render-helper
#| include: false
render_rd <- function(...) {
  rd_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".Rd")
  writeLines(
    c("\\name{tool}\\alias{tool}\\title{tool}\\description{A tool.}", ...),
    rd_file
  )
  text_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
  tools::Rd2txt(
    rd_file,
    out = text_file,
    options = list(underline_titles = FALSE)
  )
  cat(readLines(text_file), sep = "\n")
}
```

Put that text straight into a help page, and this is what readers get:

```{r}
#| label: raw-help-broken
render_rd(
  "\\section{Command line help}{",
  "\\preformatted{", raw_help, "}",
  "}"
)
```

Everything from `%` onwards is gone, because `%` starts a comment in Rd.
Braces and backslashes cause similar trouble.
Real help output is full of all three, and you only find out when a page renders wrong or not at all.

There are other ways it goes wrong that are easier to miss.
The tool might print colour codes or terminal bold.
It might hang.
And on CRAN's machines it is almost certainly not installed, so a call that errors there breaks the PDF manual, and `R CMD check` with it.

## `cli_help_rd()`

`cli_help_rd()` runs the tool and returns its help as Rd markup that is safe to put in a page.
To keep this vignette runnable everywhere, we'll use `Rscript` as the tool, since every R installation has one.

```{r}
#| label: cli-help-rd
rscript <- file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript")
help_rd <- cli_help_rd(rscript, "--help")
cat(substr(help_rd, 1, 200))
```

It wraps the output in `\preformatted{}`, escapes it, and strips terminal formatting.
When the tool isn't there, it returns a notice instead of an error:

```{r}
#| label: missing-tool
cat(cli_help_rd("mri_convert", "--help"))
```

A tool that hangs is stopped after five seconds (change it with `timeout`), and whatever it printed by then is shown, marked as cut off.

## Using it in roxygen2

roxygen2 8.0.0 added inline `Rd` code, which writes the `\Sexpr` for you.
With markdown enabled, a wrapper's documentation looks like this:

```r
#' Convert MRI volumes
#'
#' @section Command line help:
#' `Rd ventro::cli_help_rd("mri_convert", "--help")`
#' @importFrom ventro cli_help_rd
#' @export
mri_convert <- function(...) {
  ...
}
```

Add ventro to `Imports` in `DESCRIPTION`.
The `@importFrom` line only needs to appear once in your package.
Without it, `R CMD check` notes that ventro is imported but never used, because the only call to it lives inside the Rd files.

Here is the Rd that roxygen2 writes, rendered the way `?mri_convert` would show it, with `Rscript` standing in for `mri_convert`:

```{r}
#| label: rendered-page
render_rd(
  "\\section{Command line help}{",
  sprintf(
    "\\Sexpr[stage=render,results=rd]{ventro::cli_help_rd(%s, \"--help\")}",
    deparse(rscript)
  ),
  "}"
)
```

## Tools that aren't on `PATH`

Plenty of tools need more than a name to run.
FreeSurfer, for example, lives wherever `FREESURFER_HOME` points, and its programs expect that variable to be set.

`locate` takes a function that finds the tool.
It gets the command name and returns a path, a list with `path` and `env`, or `NULL` when the tool can't be found:

```r
find_freesurfer_tool <- function(command) {
  home <- Sys.getenv("FREESURFER_HOME")
  if (!nzchar(home)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  list(
    path = file.path(home, "bin", command),
    env = c(FREESURFER_HOME = home)
  )
}
```

In roxygen, pass it by name, so the call is resolved when the help page is rendered:

```r
#' `Rd ventro::cli_help_rd("mri_convert", "--help", locate = "mypkg::find_freesurfer_tool")`
```

The locator should be the same function your wrappers use to find the tool.
That way the help page and the function call can't disagree about which installation they mean.

## When something goes wrong

Every failure shows the same notice.
That's deliberate: a reader of the help page shouldn't see a stack trace.
It's less helpful when you're the one trying to work out why your locator isn't finding anything.
Set `ventro.debug` and the notice says why:

```{r}
#| label: debug
options(ventro.debug = TRUE)
broken_locator <- function(command) stop("FREESURFER_HOME points nowhere")
cat(cli_help_rd("mri_convert", locate = broken_locator))
options(ventro.debug = NULL)
```

## The `@clihelp` shorthand

If you'd rather not write the inline code, or you're on roxygen2 older than 8.0.0, ventro also provides a roxygen tag.
Turn it on in `DESCRIPTION`:

```
Imports: ventro
Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE, packages = "ventro")
```

Then one line per tool:

```r
#' @clihelp mri_convert --help
```

The tag writes the section and the `importFrom()` for you.
It also reads two package-wide settings from `DESCRIPTION`, so you don't repeat them in every block:

```
Config/ventro/title: Options for \code{{command}}
Config/ventro/locate: mypkg::find_freesurfer_tool
```

The tradeoff is that its arguments are split on whitespace, so a single argument can't contain a space.
For those, use the inline form.

## When the help is generated

In the dynamic help that R and RStudio use by default, the tool runs each time the page is opened.
Static HTML help (`R CMD INSTALL --html`) and the PDF manual are built once, so they show the tool as it was on the machine that installed the package or built the manual.
On CRAN that usually means the "not available" notice.
For a pkgdown site, it means the help of whatever is installed where the site is built, which is worth keeping in mind if you build it on CI.
